problem: BeBee needs a deterministic repository/tooling contract for generated files, source placement, text/lint conventions, dependency/license intake and canonical commands before later P0 runtime systems expand the codebase.

decision.rationale: Use Defold-aware repository metadata plus a machine-readable contract and Python-stdlib validator. This enforces fresh-clone standards without introducing a floating formatter/linter dependency solely to police repository hygiene.

research.candidate_pool_exception: Shipped-game competitor research is not applicable to repository/tooling policy; current Defold documentation/source is the relevant authority.
research.reference_exception: Official Defold editor, library and licensing documentation/source define the relevant engine/tool constraints for this task.

anti_pattern.observation: A dependency can be introduced through game.project as a remote library URL, while moving/unreviewed dependency references move code outside the repository's reviewed source state.
anti_pattern.lesson: Require every Defold library URL to match a reviewed, versioned dependency/license manifest entry and reject unregistered or stale entries.

official_docs.verified_constraint: Current Defold editor source requires /.editor_settings, /.internal and /build to be ignored by Git.
Defold editor integrates Luacheck and supports a project-root .luacheckrc; BeBee records the documented compatible baseline explicitly.
Defold library dependencies are configured as remote library archive URLs, making exact source/version registration part of reproducible repository policy.
Defold engine use/distribution is license-governed and therefore belongs in the project third-party inventory rather than being treated as no third-party technology.
Defold tools include licensed third-party components, reinforcing explicit build-tool provenance and review.

alternatives.reason: Adding formatter/linter packages now creates new version/install/license surfaces before a concrete code-quality problem requires them; repository hygiene can be enforced without that dependency cost.
Prose-only standards are weak for autonomous development because generated output, source placement and dependency registration can drift without a failing check.
Provides machine-checkable source/layout/dependency/text rules on a fresh clone with Python and Git only while retaining Defold editor Luacheck integration.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Defold editor/build state and BeBee generated roots are ignored and tracked generated output is rejected.
Formatting/lint conventions are explicit and mechanically checkable without adding an unpinned formatting dependency.
Production Defold/runtime resources have stable canonical source roots and misplaced resources fail validation.
Third-party dependency/license intake is explicit, records existing Defold/Bob technology, and game.project library URLs cannot bypass the inventory.
Repository standards and existing development/release build commands are documented and the standards command runs in CI.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/19-repository-tooling-standards.md and .github/workflows/repository-standards.yml; exact-head CI must be green before merge

automated: Repository standards workflow runs python3 scripts/check_repository_standards.py against the exact PR head.
Trusted-base validate-pr-evidence must pass on the exact final PR head before merge.
Existing Defold runtime evidence remains the authority for the BB-001 build path where its path trigger applies.
manual: Reviewed BB-002 diff for scope: no semantic input, collection-proxy lifecycle, storage, gameplay, UI or data/test harness implementation is introduced.
Reviewed dependency ledger against the already-pinned Defold 1.13.1/Bob toolchain and authoritative Defold license/tool-license sources.
verification.runtime_errors: No player runtime behavior is introduced. Merge requires exact-head repository/evidence CI success.
verification.save_data_impact: None; BB-002 introduces no persistent game state or migration.

provenance.artifact_locator: N/A — repository/tooling-only task with no player-facing rendering change

findings: The implementation is scoped to repository/tooling policy and adds a failing mechanical gate rather than relying on prose alone.
No BB-003 through BB-007 runtime capability is implemented or claimed by the standards layer.

governance.trust_boundary_change: Adds a read-only pull_request/push repository-standards workflow that executes candidate-owned validation code. It is an additional quality signal only: it does not replace, modify or weaken the pull_request_target trusted-base validate-pr-evidence policy, branch/ruleset requirements or evidence trust boundary.
governance.bypass_analysis: The new standards workflow can be changed by a candidate PR because it validates candidate repository policy; therefore it is not treated as a trusted security boundary. Governance-critical enforcement remains in the existing trusted-base workflow/policy. The validator uses git ls-files so ignored/untracked local output cannot masquerade as reviewed repository content, and dependency URLs are checked bidirectionally against the manifest.
governance.rollback: Revert the BB-002 merge to remove the standards workflow/config/validator and restore the previous THIRD_PARTY/roadmap documentation. No save data or runtime migration is involved.

known_limitations: Standalone command-line Luacheck/formatter packages are intentionally not mandatory in BB-002; Defold editor lint plus the dependency-free repository gate is the current baseline.
BB-003 owns semantic input and proxy/input-focus proof; BB-004 owns test/data harness; BB-005 owns full PR HTML5 CI; BB-006 owns deterministic visual capture; BB-007 owns storage proof.
